features.basis: TP53 mutation is highly enriched in selectively killed lines across many lineages
KRAS-mutant pancreatic/colorectal/gastric lines appear among sensitive lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines are enriched in the sensitive set
EGFR-mutant NSCLC and esophageal lines are among the most killed
PTEN loss occurs in several sensitive thyroid, glioma, kidney, and melanoma lines
NF1-mutant thyroid, glioma, and sarcoma lines appear in the sensitive group
RB1 loss is seen in sensitive thyroid, pancreatic, and gastric lines
ABCC8/SUR1 is the direct repaglinide target and KATP channel dependence may mediate sensitivity
KCNJ11/Kir6.2 is the pore-forming KATP subunit targeted by repaglinide
PPARG is an annotated repaglinide target and may contribute to growth inhibition in expressing lines
OATP1B1-mediated uptake can increase intracellular exposure to repaglinide
OATP2B1 is a drug influx transporter that may enhance repaglinide uptake in expressing tumor cells

raw.explanation: Repaglinide is a meglitinide insulin secretagogue that closes ATP-sensitive potassium channels by binding the SUR1/KCNJ11-ABCC8 complex, and its selective anticancer effect likely reflects dependence of certain tumor cells on KATP channel activity or on the drug's additional targets such as PPARG and OATP-mediated uptake. The strongest pattern in the observed data is enrichment of TP53-mutant, KRAS/BRAF/EGFR/RAS-pathway-driven, and PTEN/NF1/RB1-loss lines among sensitive lines, suggesting that cells with compromised p53 and activated MAPK/PI3K survival signaling are more vulnerable to repaglinide-induced metabolic/ionic stress. Conversely, lines with intact or alternative survival wiring, including NRAS-mutant melanoma and several PIK3CA/CTNNB1-mutant gastrointestinal models, are relatively protected.
